ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, A to B is a horizontal line segment, labeled 10; B to C is an obliquely upward line segment, labeled 20; A to C is a dashed line, indicating the relevant side AC to be found. According to the problem statement, the boat turns through angle theta from the forward direction of AB and then proceeds along BC, where 45° <= theta <= 60°. In triangle ABC, the interior angle at point B is 180° - theta. By the law of cosines: AC^2 = 10^2 + 20^2 - 2(10)(20)cos(180° - theta). Because cos(180° - theta) = -cos(theta), AC^2 = 500 + 400cos(theta). When theta goes from 45° to 60°, cos(theta) decreases from sqrt(2)/2 to 1/2, so AC^2 goes from 500 + 400(1/2) = 700 to 500 + 400(sqrt(2)/2) ≈ 782.8. This range is contained in the interval [700,800].
